plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no incentive to shade my bid down or up. Bidding exactly my value of $39 maximizes my expected profit: I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids, and I pay less than my value, ensuring non-negative profit whenever I win.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I win only if I'm highest, and pay the second-highest bid (not my own), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $20, so I will bid exactly $20 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value (negative profit). If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $20.
